subject: zoology
question_text: What are the features peculiar to ratite birds? Give two examples of ratite birds.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.65, Star Questions Plus, SAQ 182). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK ERRORS: the book's numbered list runs 1,2,3,4,5,8,7,6,9,10,11 — the numbers 6, 7 and 8 are printed out of order (a harmless printing slip; the card renumbers them). The book prints 'Dromaeus' and the common name 'Kiwi'; the accepted genus names are Dromaius and Apteryx, and the card uses those.

steps.why: Every other ratite feature follows from the flat keel-less sternum, so the sternum is written first and the rest of the answer is read off it.
common_mistakes: Writing that ratite birds have a keel. The keel is exactly what they lack; carinate birds have it.
Calling them primitive birds that never flew. They are MODERN birds whose ancestors could fly.
steps.memory_tip: Ratis means raft: a flat raft of a breast bone, so no muscles, so no flight.

steps.why: A bird that does not fly loses every part that only flight needed, so the missing hooklets, pygostyle and furcula are one idea told three times.
common_mistakes: Writing that ratite feathers are absent. They are present but loose, with no hooklets.
Saying the wish bone is present. The clavicles are absent, so no furcula is formed.
steps.memory_tip: No flight, so no flight parts: loose feathers, no pygostyle, no wish bone.

steps.label: Other peculiar features
steps.margin_note: Four short features. The precocial line is the one most often left out.

steps.why: The copulatory organ and the precocial chicks are the two features that are NOT losses, so they are the ones that mark a ratite as its own group rather than a damaged flier.
common_mistakes: Writing that ratite young are helpless at hatching. They are precocial and run early.
Saying all birds have a copulatory organ. In most birds it is absent; in ratites the male has one.
steps.memory_tip: Two absent (syrinx, preen gland) and two present (copulatory organ, running chicks).

steps.label: Distribution and examples
steps.margin_note: Two examples are asked; naming two with their homes is enough for the mark.

steps.why: The birds are flightless yet spread across separated southern continents, which is why the distribution is called discontinuous and is a marked feature and not a stray fact.
common_mistakes: Naming a penguin as a ratite. A penguin is flightless but has a keeled sternum, so it is carinate.
Giving the country and not the genus. The scientific name is what carries the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Five ratites on five southern lands: Rhea, Struthio, Dromaius, Casuarius, Apteryx.

insider_note: The keel is the whole question — an answer that says flightless without the words raft like sternum without a keel loses the mark that every examiner marks first.
